title: Democrats Are Gearing Up to Investigate the Trump Administration. It Won’t Be Easy
gist: With polls suggesting Democrats could win the House and possibly the Senate, the article argues congressional oversight of the Trump administration faces steep obstacles: agencies stonewalled a GAO report on DOGE, and Congress's enforcement tools (subpoenas, contempt, courts, the purse, confirmations) are weak or slow. Legal expert Emily Berman concludes 'there are no good options'.

themes.theme: Power of the purse and confirmations

insights.claim: Jamie Raskin says Congress has the power of the purse to pressure the executive into complying with investigations, but this is a blunt tool because funding is bundled in omnibus bills that mix routine operations with administration priorities.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Funding fights tied to oversight raise shutdown risk; watch appropriations deadlines under a divided government.

insights.claim: Senate Democrats' refusal to pass an appropriations bill funding DHS after the killing of Alex Pretti by two CBP agents in Minnesota led to a months-long partial government shutdown, with unpaid TSA workers and major airport delays.
insights.speaker: Vittoria Elliott
insights.so_what: Precedent that funding leverage causes broad collateral damage (air travel) and could recur around future appropriations.
